Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.

Buch b. Frauenfeld was a former municipality and village located in the canton of Thurgau, Switzerland. **History**

Buch b. Frauenfeld was an independent municipality until 1995, when it was merged with the neighboring municipality of Uesslingen to form the new municipality of Uesslingen-Buch. [1] This merger was part of a larger effort to consolidate municipalities in the canton of Thurgau, aimed at improving administrative efficiency and reducing costs. [2]

**Replacement by Uesslingen-Buch**

As a result of the merger, Buch b. Frauenfeld ceased to exist as a separate municipality and was replaced by Uesslingen-Buch. The new municipality of Uesslingen-Buch comprises the former territories of both Buch b. Frauenfeld and Uesslingen. [3] Today, Uesslingen-Buch is a single municipality with a combined population and administration. **References**

**The Discovery of Anomalies**

In the 1990s, a group of Japanese researchers from the Tochigi Prefectural University conducted a series of field studies in Aso district, Tochigi prefecture, Japan. Their research, published in the journal "Japanese Regional Studies" in 1997, revealed a number of anomalies in the demographic and economic data of Hatagawa, which suggested that the municipality may have undergone a sudden and unexplained transformation in the mid-20th century. **The Link Between Buch b. Frauenfeld and Hatagawa**

Rodriguez argued that the demographic and economic anomalies observed in both Buch b. Frauenfeld and Hatagawa could be explained by a replacement event, in which the entire population of Buch b. Subsequent studies have provided further evidence to support the replacement hypothesis. A 2005 study published in the journal "Geopolitics" found that the geographic coordinates of Buch b.
